requirements.requirement: node1 (VyOS) is configured as router between lan-a (node2) and lan-b (node3), with functioning routing between the two networks
requirements.summary: node1 eth1/eth2 assigned 10.50.50.254/24 and 10.50.60.254/24, ip_forward and per-interface forwarding enabled, node2/node3 given static IPs and explicit routes via node1 fixing a default-route metric asymmetry, and cross-LAN reachability confirmed via ping showing traffic transits node1.

requirements.requirement: node2 (lan-a) is allowed to reach node3 (lan-b) on TCP port 5432
requirements.summary: VyOS forward filter rule 10 accepts tcp/5432 from eth1 to eth2; node3 firewalld public zone (which otherwise blocks all inbound) was opened with a rich rule for tcp/5432 from 10.50.50.0/24. A stand-in socat listener on port 5432 (no real postgres present) verified actual TCP connectivity from node2, succeeding both before and after all three nodes were restarted.

requirements.requirement: All other traffic between lan-a and lan-b is rejected, in both directions
requirements.summary: VyOS forward filter default-action is drop with only an established/related accept and the tcp/5432 eth1->eth2 accept rule. Verified directly: a non-5432 TCP port (8080) blocked lan-a->lan-b, ICMP blocked lan-a->lan-b, and TCP/5432 plus ICMP blocked in the reverse direction (lan-b->lan-a). Re-confirmed after node2's restart (8080 still blocked) and after all restarts (ping still blocked).

overall_summary: The task's material outcomes, node1 routing between lan-a/lan-b, node2 allowed to reach node3:5432, and all other cross-LAN traffic rejected in both directions, are all directly and repeatedly demonstrated via real TCP/ICMP probes, not just configuration inspection. Independently, the provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol was executed competently on all three nodes: each shows a pre-restart boot_id/healthy baseline, an explicit restart command, a changed post-restart boot_id (cross-checked against the fixed after-prepare/after-executor snapshots, which agree), and re-verification of interface, route, firewall, and firewalld state plus end-to-end 5432-allow/other-traffic-block behavior after each reboot.
limitations: No real PostgreSQL service was present in the image; connectivity verification relied on a temporary socat stand-in listener on port 5432, a reasonable substitute but not identical to verifying an actual database service.

The before_prepare and after_prepare snapshots are identical (prepare phase disabled/aliased), so preparer-vs-executor state separation relies entirely on comparing before_prepare against after_executor.

operational_hygiene.summary: Mutations were largely scoped to satisfying the task: VyOS interface/firewall config, node2/node3 static IP and route assignment, and node3's firewalld rich rule (a necessary prerequisite since its default zone blocked all inbound traffic). One early firewall commit attempt using invalid state-flag syntax failed and left no committed change (cmd-466b34a3bd1342c7), corrected immediately afterward (cmd-966608b8d68343b6), a harmless troubleshooting iteration. The socat TCP/5432 (and a transient 8080) listeners deployed on node3/node2 as postgres stand-ins are reasonable given no real postgres service exists in the image, and were largely cleaned up (node2's 5432 listener killed via cmd-7756e2cd59bf4d6a; node3's 8080 listener killed via cmd-4461acd38eb24780), but node3's 5432 socat listener was intentionally left running (and restarted after reboot in cmd-eaaac37454ba48fc) as ongoing evidence of the allowed service, a low-risk, disclosed piece of test scaffolding rather than unexplained residue, though retained in final state rather than fully removed.
